motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Primary transition curve for UI enter/exit (150ms-250ms, strictly < 300ms). Never use ease-in or transition: all.

motion.name: ease-sheet
motion.purpose: Deceleration curve for full-width mobile bottom sheets and drawers (200ms-240ms).

motion.name: spring-release-snap

motion.name: ease-in-out

narrative.overview:
The visual world of 711acks reflects the ambient warmth, late-night quietude, and distinct glow of an after-hours 7-Eleven in the Philippines, reframed through a disciplined, high-craft editorial lens. Rather than mimicking commercial retail noise or adopting generic SaaS card templates, the interface treats beverage hacks as handcrafted discoveries. Deep cypress tones, obsidian shadows, and linen backgrounds provide a rich, tactile canvas illuminated by razor-sharp citron accents and soft light reveals.

Every screen balances high-utility mobile scanability with cinematic atmosphere. The dual-theme 'Midnight Green' architecture transitions seamlessly between the warm daylight of Linen Cream (#F5F3EC) and the immersive nighttime depth of Obsidian Midnight (#17201B). Subtle micro-spring presses, 44px minimum touch targets, and fine-pointer hover lifts give the application a physical, responsive presence that honors convenience-store immediacy without sacrificing editorial restraint.
keyCharacteristics: Atmospheric lighting and multi-stop eased gradients that eliminate banding
Oversized ultra-light display typography paired with crystal-clear tabular figures
Translucent hairline borders and ambient depth over heavy drop shadows
High-contrast, touch-optimized ergonomics tailored for mobile convenience-store browsing
Strict separation between fan-made editorial minimalism and commercial retail clutter

rules.name: The Citron Rarity Rule
rules.body: Electric Citron Lime (#D7E07A) must never cover more than 8% of any given screen. Its power comes from scarcity—a focused beam of light directing attention to likes, active filters, and primary confirmations.

rules.name: The Heritage Stripe Rule
rules.body: The official 7-Eleven-inspired colors (Orange #F58220, Green #008061, Red #EE2526) exist strictly as a single 3px decorative hairline in the site footer. They are never permitted on buttons, cards, or hero elements, preserving the project's independent identity.

rules.name: The Tabular Price Rule
rules.body: Every currency figure, purchase cost, and quantity count must strictly render in JetBrains Mono or enforce font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums (tabular-nums-strict). Figures must never jump or misalign during state changes or real-time calculations.

rules.name: The Light Display Rule
rules.body: Display headings larger than 24px must always use font weights of 300 or lighter. Heavy display weights create brutish promotional posters; light weights create editorial luxury.

rules.name: The Hairline Depth Rule
rules.body: Depth is primarily articulated through translucent hairline borders and background tonal contrast; drop shadows never cast harsh black cutouts.

rules.name: The Fine-Pointer Hover Rule
rules.body: Transform lifts (translate3d(0, -2px, 0)) and card-zoom effects (scale(1.04)) are strictly scoped inside @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine). Mobile touch screens never trigger sticky hover states.

rules.name: The Pressable Feedback Rule
rules.body: All interactive elements must implement the .pressable utility, applying GPU-accelerated scaling (transform: scale(0.97)) on :active with a snappy 160ms ease-out curve (cubic-bezier(0.165, 0.84, 0.44, 1)).

rules.name: The Sub-300ms Transition Rule
rules.body: All standard UI interface transitions must complete in under 300ms (targeted 150ms–250ms). Animations exist to clarify physical state changes, never to entertain or keep users waiting.

rules.name: The Compositor-Only Rule
rules.body: Animations must touch only transform, opacity, or sub-20px filter: blur. Any animation touching layout or box-model dimensions is rejected during review.

rules.name: The Zero-Rerender Gesture Rule
rules.body: High-frequency pointer and touch move handlers must never call React setState. Store live coordinates in mutable refs and write styles directly to element refs.

rules.name: The Velocity-Seeded Dismiss Rule
rules.body: Bottom sheets dismiss on ≥40% displacement or >500px/s flick velocity. Subtle spring bounce is isolated strictly to physical drag snap-backs; button and Escape closes remain bounce-free.

dos: Do display all product prices and total purchase sums in Philippine Pesos (₱) using strict tabular numeric typography.
Do enforce an invisible 44x44px minimum hit target (.hit-target-44) on all touch targets regardless of their visible visual size.
Do constrain all UI transitions to 150ms–250ms (strictly < 300ms) using cubic-bezier(0.165, 0.84, 0.44, 1).
Do animate only GPU-accelerated compositor properties (transform, opacity, and micro-blurs < 20px).
Do track touch and pointer gestures 1:1 with zero artificial easing and zero React re-renders during drag events.
Do dismiss swipeable modals when drag displacement reaches ≥ 40% or downward flick velocity exceeds 500px/s.
Do isolate spring bounce strictly to physical drag release snap-backs (keeping button/Escape closes bounce-free).
Do use multi-stop eased gradients (at least 4 stops) whenever overlaying dark scrims on food and beverage photography.
Do honor reduced motion preferences by canceling spring transforms and auto-scroll behaviors under @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce).
Do keep product ingredient cards focused on commercial shelf packaging photos and full-unit retail pricing.
donts: Don't use ease-in timing curves or blanket transition: all.
Don't animate layout geometry such as width, height, top, left, padding, or margin.
Don't trigger React state re-renders inside pointermove or touchmove gesture loops.
Don't add spring bounces to programmatic button clicks or keyboard Escape dismissals.
Don't use standard two-stop linear gradients that create harsh banding edges over dark backgrounds.
Don't attach hover effects (:hover) without qualifying @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine).
Don't apply heavy drop shadows or colored glow halos that distract from clean photographic packaging assets.
Don't use official 7-Eleven logos, trademarked slogans, or official promotional badge graphics.
Don't introduce step-by-step recipe cooking tutorials, difficulty meters, or prep-time badges.
